original_question: For n > m > 1, let S(m, n) mean that every n-fold self-joining whose projections to all m-dimensional faces of X^n equal mu^m is trivial, that is, equal to mu^n, and let S_n denote S(n - 1, n). How are the odd properties S_{2n-1} related to one another?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Q8: “How are the odd properties S_{2n-1} related to one another?” This question is posed immediately after the paper defines S(m,n) and introduces the shorthand S_n:=S(n-1,n). ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it uses the same self-joining property S(m,n), the same abbreviation S_n:=S(n-1,n), and it asks precisely about the odd properties S_{2n-1}, which is the official open problem Q8 in §2. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
missing_details: The paper asks this for a measure-preserving action/dynamical system; the object having property S(m,n) should be named explicitly, not just the measure space (X,μ). ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

An n-fold self-joining should be made explicit as a T^{×n}-invariant probability measure on X^n with one-coordinate marginals μ. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

The phrase “all m-dimensional faces” means all m-coordinate projections (the m-dimensional coordinate faces of the n-cube), each required to equal μ^m. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

The nearby context in the paper is part of the intended scope: all even properties are already known to be mutually equivalent and to imply all odd properties, so the open problem is specifically about the relations among odd properties themselves. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

Immediately after Q8, the paper notes that there are group actions having all odd properties but not the even property, so the refined question should not drift into asking whether odd properties imply the even ones. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
refined_question: Let T be a measure-preserving action on a probability space (X,μ). For integers n>m>1, say that T has property S(m,n) if every n-fold self-joining λ of T—that is, every T^{×n}-invariant probability measure on X^n with one-coordinate marginals μ—whose projection to every m-dimensional coordinate face of X^n equals μ^m is trivial, i.e. λ=μ^n; write S_n:=S(n-1,n). It is known that the even properties S_{2k} are all mutually equivalent and imply every odd property S_{2ℓ-1}. What implication or equivalence relations hold among the odd properties S_3,S_5,S_7,… themselves? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Q8 in §2. The definition of S(m,n) and the shorthand S_n are given immediately before Q8, and the surrounding sentences supply the paper-faithful scope: even properties are already known to be equivalent and to force the odd ones, while examples exist of group actions with all odd properties but no even property. Therefore the sharp stand-alone version should ask only for the mutual implication structure among the odd properties for a measure-preserving action, without broadening to neighboring problems about PID, MSJ, entropy, or multiple mixing. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
